pass_a_gloss: Next, after the discourse concerning the two peoples, of the former to whom the threat is given, and of the latter to whom the promise is given, he says (that is, he spoke evidently to the former): 'And now I spoke to the men of Judah and to those dwelling in Jerusalem: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am fashioning against you evil. For in my hand these things which I am fashioning against you are able to be scattered. Do these things to be scattered from my hand, so that the evil things which I am fashioning against you I may change and do good. You would not find—behold, I am fashioning against you good' and the things spoken of them in order according to reason, so that after this he might show that the things which he fashions good he releases from the hands, in order that he might make them evil. But he fashions evil according to the said example, and fashioning evil he manages (apart from the interpretation of the given 'fell from my hands'), so that if it falls, and the end of the things being fashioned evil I do not know what kind it will become.
source_text: Ἑξῆς μετὰ τὸν περὶ τῶν δύο ἐθνῶν λόγον, τοῦ προτέρου ᾧ ἡ ἀπειλὴ δίδοται, καὶ τοῦ δευτέρου ᾧ ἡ ἐπαγγελία δίδοται, φησίν (εἶπε δηλονότι τοῖς προτέροις)· «καὶ νῦν εἶπον πρὸς ἄνδρας Ἰούδα καὶ πρὸς τοὺς κατοικοῦντας Ἱερουσαλήμ· οὕτως λέγει κύριος· ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ πλάσσω ἐφ᾿ ὐμᾶς κακά. ὅτι ἐν τῇ χειρί μου ταῦτά ἐστιν ἃ πλάσσω ἐφ᾿ ὑμᾶς, δύναται διαπεσεῖν. ποιήσατε ταῦτα διαπεσεῖν ἀπὸ τῆς χειρός μου, ἵνα ἃ πλάσσω ἐφ᾿ ὑμᾶς κακὰ μεταβάλω καὶ ποιήσω ἀγαθά. οὐκ ἂν εὕροις· >ἰδοὺ πλάσσω ἐφ᾿ ὑμᾶς ἀγαθά< καὶ τὰ ἀνὰ λόγον αὐτῶν λεγόμενα ἑξῆς, ἵνα μετὰ τοῦτο ἐμφήνῃ ὅτι ἃ πλάσσει ἀγαθὰ ἀπολύει ἀπὸ τῶν χειρῶν, ἵνα ποιήσῃ αὐτὰ κακά. ἀλλὰ πλάσσει κακὰ κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον παράδειγμα, καὶ πλάσσων κακὰ οἰκονομεῖ (χωρὶς τῆς ἑρμηνείας τῆς ἀποδεδομένης εἰς τὸ «ἔπεσεν ἀπὸ τῶν χειρῶν μου«), ἵνα ἐὰν πέσῃ, καὶ τὸ τέλος τῶν πλασσομένων κακῶν οὐκ οἶδα ποταπὸν γένηται.
pass_b_english: Next after the word about the two nations—the former to which the threat is given, and the second to which the promise is given—he says (clearly he spoke to the former): 'And now I said to men of Judah and to those inhabiting Jerusalem: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I fashion evils upon you.' (Jeremiah 18:11) Because these things which I fashion upon you are in my hand, they can fall away. Make these things fall away from my hand, that I may change the evils which I fashion upon you and do goods.

You would not find: 'Behold, I fashion goods upon you' (Jeremiah 18:6) and the things said next according to their proportion, that after this he might show that the goods which he fashions he releases from the hands, in order to make them evils. But he fashions evils according to the example said, and fashioning evils he manages (apart from the interpretation already given into 'it fell from my hands' (Jeremiah 18:8)), so that if it falls, even the end of the evils being fashioned—I do not know of what sort it may become (Jeremiah 18:10).
